info.name: BookLeaf Author Support API
info.description:
REST API for the BookLeaf Author Support & Communication Portal.

## Getting started
1. Check the collection **Variables** tab. `BASE_URL` defaults to local; set it to `https://api.bookleaf.code26.site` for production.
2. Run **Auth → Login as Author** or **Auth → Login as Admin**.
3. Call requests in that role’s folder. Ids are saved into variables as you go.

## Authentication
Login sets the HTTP-only `bl_session` cookie (Postman sends it automatically) and returns a `csrfToken`, saved to `CSRF_TOKEN`. Every POST/PATCH under a session sends it in the `X-CSRF-Token` header. A missing or wrong token returns `403 CSRF_TOKEN_INVALID`.

## Responses
- Success: `{ "success": true, "data": ... }`; paginated lists add `meta: { page, pageSize, total, totalPages }`
- Error: `{ "success": false, "error": { "code", "message", "details?", "requestId" } }`

Error codes: `VALIDATION_ERROR`, `UNAUTHENTICATED`, `INVALID_CREDENTIALS`, `SESSION_EXPIRED`, `CSRF_TOKEN_INVALID`, `FORBIDDEN`, `NOT_FOUND`, `CONFLICT`, `INVALID_STATE_TRANSITION`, `RATE_LIMITED`, `AI_UNAVAILABLE`, `PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE`, `INTERNAL_ERROR`, `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`.

item.name: Health
item.description: Public routes with no session. Use `/health` for uptime monitors.

request.description: Landing response with the API name, version and links to `/health` and `/api/v1`.

Returns **200** `{"status":"ok"}` when the server and MongoDB are both up, and **503** `{"status":"degraded"}` otherwise. The response includes `uptimeSeconds`, `database.connected`, `database.state` and `timestamp`.

exec: pm.test('API and database are up', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));

item.name: Auth
item.description:
Login sets the HTTP-only `bl_session` cookie, which Postman stores and sends automatically, and returns a `csrfToken`. The login scripts save that token to `CSRF_TOKEN`.

There is **one session at a time** per `BASE_URL`, because both roles use the same cookie. Run **Login as Author** before the Author folder and **Login as Admin** before the Admin folder.

Login is rate-limited. Repeated failures return `429 RATE_LIMITED`.

request.description: Signs in with `AUTHOR_EMAIL` / `AUTHOR_PASSWORD` and saves `CSRF_TOKEN`.
Signs in with `ADMIN_EMAIL` / `ADMIN_PASSWORD` and saves `CSRF_TOKEN` and `ADMIN_USER_ID`, which the assign request uses.
Returns the signed-in user, a fresh `csrfToken` and `expiresAt`, and saves the token again. Returns `401` without a session.
Clears the session cookie. Works even when the session has already expired.

item.name: Author
item.description: Requires **Login as Author**. Admin sessions get `403 FORBIDDEN` here.

item.name: Profile & Books
item.description: Scoped to the signed-in author. The author comes from the session, never from the request.

request.description: Author code, name, email, phone, city and joined date.
Totals for books, copies sold, royalties earned/paid/pending and open tickets, plus the royalty payout calendar and a short book list.

query.description: Search by title, book code or ISBN (max 100 chars).

request.description: Paginated. Saves the first book code to `BOOK_CODE` if it is empty.
One book by its book code, such as `BK001`. Returns `404` for books that belong to another author.

item.name: Tickets
item.description: Tickets raised by the signed-in author. Authors only ever see the public conversation, never internal notes.

header.description: Saved by the login requests. Required on every POST/PATCH under a session.

request.description:
Creates a ticket and saves its id to `TICKET_ID`. AI triage runs in the background, so creation never waits on the AI.

- `bookId`: a book code such as `BK001`, or `null` for a general/account-level question
- `subject`: 5 to 150 characters
- `description`: 20 to 5000 characters

Rate-limited per author.

query.description: Subject or ticket reference such as `BL-1001`.

request.description: Paginated. Saves the first ticket id to `TICKET_ID` if it is empty.
Ticket detail with the public conversation and `canReply`. Returns `404` for tickets that belong to another author.

header.description: Saved by the login requests. Required on every POST/PATCH under a session.

request.description: Adds a follow-up message (1 to 10000 characters). A reply on a `RESOLVED` ticket re-opens it; a `CLOSED` ticket returns `409`.
Server-Sent Events stream of the author’s own ticket events. Events carry ids only; fetch the ticket for details. The connection stays open, so stop it manually.

item.name: Admin
item.description: Requires **Login as Admin**. Author sessions get `403 FORBIDDEN` here.

item.name: Dashboard & Directory
item.description: Operations dashboard, author directory and the admin user list.

request.description: Ticket counts by status and urgency, average first-response time, unresolved tickets by category, the needs-attention list, recent activity and AI usage over the last 24 hours.

query.description: Name, email or author code (max 100 chars).

request.description: Paginated author directory with book and open-ticket counts. Saves the first author id to `AUTHOR_ID` if it is empty.
Author profile with their books, tickets and royalty totals.
Active admins, used by the assignee picker. Saves the first id to `ADMIN_USER_ID` if it is empty.
Server-Sent Events stream of every ticket event. The connection stays open, so stop it manually.

item.name: Tickets
item.description:
The operations queue and ticket workspace.

Allowed status changes: `OPEN` → `IN_PROGRESS`/`RESOLVED`/`CLOSED`; `IN_PROGRESS` → `OPEN`/`RESOLVED`/`CLOSED`; `RESOLVED` → `IN_PROGRESS`/`CLOSED`; `CLOSED` → `IN_PROGRESS`. Any other change returns `409 INVALID_STATE_TRANSITION`.

query.description: Subject, author name/email/code or reference such as `BL-1001`.
Created on or after this date (YYYY-MM-DD).
Created on or before this date (YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive).

request.description: Paginated queue with server-side filtering and sorting (default sort: `urgency`). Saves the first ticket id to `TICKET_ID`, replacing any earlier value.
Full workspace data: description, author profile, book detail, triage result, messages, internal notes, activity, the cached AI draft and `allowedTransitions`.

request.description:
Sends a public reply to the author (1 to 10000 characters).

- `statusAfter`: `IN_PROGRESS` or `RESOLVED` (optional; defaults to `IN_PROGRESS` for open tickets)
- `draftId`: the AI draft the reply started from, or `null`. It records whether the reply was manual, an edited draft or an unedited draft.

Returns `409` when the ticket is `CLOSED`.

item.name: AI Configuration
item.description:
AI status, knowledge base, run log and versioned strategies.

Strategy kinds: `CLASSIFICATION` (global, `category` must be `null`), `PRIORITY` and `RESPONSE` (both need a `category`). Every config save creates a new immutable version.

request.description: Whether a provider is configured, the default models for triage and drafting, circuit-breaker state and usage over the last 24 hours.
The knowledge-base sections the AI uses to ground drafts.
Paginated log of AI calls with latency, token usage and failures.
All strategies with their active config and run stats. Saves the first id to `STRATEGY_ID` if it is empty.

header.description: Saved by the login requests. Required on every POST/PATCH under a session.

request.description: Creates a strategy at version 1 and saves its id to `STRATEGY_ID`. Returns `409` if one already exists for that kind and category.
